paragraphs: (a) Son of R. Gamliel son of R. Yehudah HaNasi, our holy Rabbi. He was an amora. He and his court voted concerning gentile oil and permitted it. Rav would not eat it. Shmuel told him, “Eat; otherwise I will write against you that you are a rebellious elder.” He pressed him, and he ate, as in Avodah Zarah: Jerusalem Ein Maamidin, halakhah 9 [Avodah Zarah 2:8 in the checked edition]; Shabbat 1:4; Babylonian Avodah Zarah 35b, Mishnah, “Rabbi and his court permitted the oil.” Rashi explains that we do not read Rabbi, because his grandson R. Yehudah Nesia permitted it, as in the Gemara, 37a: Yehudah Nesia walked leaning on the shoulder of his attendant R. Simlai and said, “Simlai, were you not in the study house last night when we permitted the oil?” The Gemara's R. Yehudah Nesia is the son of R. Gamliel son of Rabbi, in amoraic times. We likewise say R. Yehudah HaNasi, son of R. Gamliel, ruled, etc.; Rabbi himself was R. Shimon ben Gamliel's son. End of quotation. Tosafot there, 36a, likewise writes: “Rashi writes on the Mishnah not to read ‘Rabbi and his court permitted the oil,’ since R. Yehudah HaNasi, his grandson, and his court permitted it. His generation's sages inserted this in the Mishnah arranged by his grandfather Rabbi. The R. Yehudah HaNasi mentioned here is R. Yehudah Nesia of amoraic times; Mishnah and baraita call him HaNasi, while amoraic language calls him Nesia. The aforementioned Jerusalem Talmud has ‘Rabbi and his court permitted the oil,’ and in three places R. Yehudah HaNasi is called ‘our teachers’: bills of divorce, oil, and the sandal. Apparently there is a scribal error: it should read ‘R. Yehudah HaNasi and his court permitted the oil, and in three places, etc.’ This is R. Yehudah Nesia.” End of Tosafot. Likewise the Mishnah at the end of Sotah, “When Rabbi died, humility and fear ceased, etc.,” was inserted by the generation's sages: Techillat Chokhmah, gate 2, rule 9. See Rabbi, R. Yehoshua ben Levi, and R. Gamliel son of our holy Rabbi above.

(b) Gittin 76b: “Our teachers permitted her to marry.” Who are our teachers? R. Yehudah said: Shmuel said: the court that permitted oil. Rashi explains: R. Yehudah Nesia, our holy Rabbi's grandson, who lived in amoraic times, as Avodah Zarah says he walked leaning, etc. R. Abba son of R. Chiyya bar Abba said: R. Yochanan said: R. Yehudah Nesia son of R. Gamliel son of Rabbi—our holy Rabbi, Rashi—ruled, but not all his company agreed; some say, “not throughout his time.” End of quotation. Jerusalem Talmud, HaMappelet and Mi SheAchazo, halakhah 3: in three places R. Yehudah HaNasi is called our teachers—bills of divorce, oil, and the sandal. Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 33b, says the Tosefta reads “R. Yehudah permitted the oil,” meaning R. Yehudah Nesia, not “Rabbi permitted it.” End of quotation. Why call him R. Yehudah HaNasi, rather than son of R. Gamliel, as R. Abba son of R. Chiyya bar Abba says, “R. Yehudah Nesia son of R. Gamliel son of Rabbi”? Elsewhere in the Talmud Nesia makes clear that he is not Rabbi. But when the Mishnah calls him R. Yehudah HaNasi, it should add son of R. Gamliel son of Rabbi to prevent confusion. One may answer that tannaim and amoraim of his time called him without qualification, since everyone knew whom they meant. Thus Rav and Shmuel, who lived in his time—see above: R. Yehudah Nesia lived in R. Yochanan's time, and R. Yochanan lived in Rav's and Shmuel's, so he did too; Tosafot, Rosh Hashanah 20, likewise says so—called him simply as if saying “our nasi, R. Yehudah.” He cannot have lived afterward, since Shmuel challenged Rav from R. Yehudah Nesia. But R. Abba son of R. Chiyya bar Abba in Gittin lived afterward and needed his father's name to prevent confusion: Maginnei Shelomoh, Chullin 5. See R. Gamliel son of Rabbi above, what I wrote there.

(c) Rabbah, Vayishlach, “Dinah, Leah's daughter, went out”: see Yefeh Toar, which writes that Rabbi—the passage says the presidents will be punished, and Rabbi became angry—is R. Yehudah Nesia. Heilprin points to Eruvin for the comparison between a generation and its leader. [The checked Yefeh Toar cites Arakhin 17a.] But Sefer Keritot, Yemot Olam, sections 5–6, says R. Yehudah HaNasi was a tanna, while R. Yehudah Nesia was an amora, R. Ammi's student, as in Avodah Zarah 33b, beginning. R. Yehudah Nesia asked R. Ammi about returning the vessels to a fiery furnace so that they became white. [The received text cites Menachot 29b. The question appears in Avodah Zarah 33b:2.] His amoraic date likewise appears from Moed Katan 17a: Rav Yehudah placed a scholar under a ban and died. The rabbis told the scholar, “No great man like Rav Yehudah is here to release you; go to R. Yehudah Nesia.” He went, and the nasi told R. Ammi to examine his case. R. Ammi thought to release him, but R. Shmuel bar Nachmani stood, etc.; see there. Yet Jerusalem HaNechenakin, halakhah 4 [Sanhedrin 11:3:5 in the checked edition], calls the tanna R. Yehudah HaNasi “R. Yehudah Nesia”: R. Yochanan said all seven qualities enumerated by the sages were fulfilled in Rabbi, namely R. Yehudah Nesia. R. Abbahu said Rabbi, R. Yehudah Nesia, and our holy Rabbi are one. Everyone agrees our holy Rabbi is Rabbi concerning gentile oil; see there, section 18. Our reading is “Who is Rabbi? R. Yehudah HaNasi.” R. Abbahu said, “He is Rabbi; he is R. Yudan HaNasi; he is our teacher.”

The statement in Sefer Keritot that R. Ammi was R. Yehudah Nesia's teacher is difficult. Why send the banned scholar to R. Yehudah Nesia rather than his teacher R. Ammi? Perhaps because he was nasi: Moed Katan says one who does not know who banned him should go to a nasi to be released. What difference whether he does not know the issuer or the issuer died? I later found it explicit in Jerusalem Megallechin, halakhah 1: if one of those who banned him dies, they do not release him. R. Yehoshua ben Levi said this applies where there is no nasi; if there is, the nasi releases him. But why say, “No great man like Rav Yehudah is here; go to R. Yehudah Nesia”? This implies that had such a great man been there, they would not have sent him to the nasi, whereas when the issuer dies a nasi is specifically required. Also, how could the nasi tell R. Ammi to examine his case, if a nasi is required? One may answer: a nasi is needed only when no one is greater than the issuer; if someone greater exists, a nasi is unnecessary. So too Beit Yosef, Yoreh Deah 334, apparently indicates. Still, why not send him to R. Ammi, the nasi's teacher? Perhaps R. Ammi was not greater than Rav Yehudah, who issued the ban. This seems likely: Dorot Olam regards Rav Yehudah as greater than Rav Huna (see there), while R. Ammi was subordinate to Rav Huna; see there. Sefer Keritot's proof that everyone agrees Rabbi permitted oil, since he is mentioned as a tanna in the Mishnah, apparently rests on its reading “R. Yehudah Nesia permitted the oil.” It therefore says the Jerusalem Talmud calls Rabbi “R. Yehudah Nesia.” You can see that its claim that Rabbi permitted oil opposes the Rashi and Tosafot quoted above.

(d) Sefer Keritot further says R. Yehudah Nesia, son of R. Gamliel son of Rabbi, was an amora and R. Ammi's student, because he asked him and told him to examine the banned scholar's case. This too opposes Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 33b, on “R. Yehudah Nesia asked R. Ammi about returning them to a fiery furnace.” Tosafot writes: “Apparently this is not the R. Yehudah Nesia who permitted oil, since that one was our holy Rabbi's grandson and appears even in a baraita: ‘Our teachers permitted her to marry.’ See the Gittin passage quoted above. Rather, he came afterward, perhaps a grandson of the R. Yehudah Nesia who decreed concerning oil [the source's wording]. He is the R. Yehudah Nesia of Moed Katan 12b, who drank water heated by an Aramean cook. Rav Assi”—it should read Rav Ammi—“heard and was angry.” End of quotation. Tosafot, Rosh Hashanah 20a, likewise says concerning R. Yehudah Nesia's message to R. Ammi, “Know that throughout R. Yochanan's life he taught us, etc.”: “This is not the R. Yehudah Nesia who permitted oil in Ein Maamidin, who lived in Rav's and Shmuel's time”—as above, Rav refused to eat until Shmuel told him to—“for that one was the son of R. Gamliel, son of R. Yehudah HaNasi. This one here was R. Yochanan's student, who was subordinate to Rav and Shmuel.” End of quotation. Tosafot thus yields that the R. Yehudah Nesia who asked R. Ammi, and to whom the banned scholar was sent, was the grandson of the R. Yehudah Nesia who was our holy Rabbi's grandson. Sefer Keritot instead regards this student of R. Ammi as R. Yehudah Nesia son of R. Gamliel son of our holy Rabbi. Beitzah 27a: R. Yehudah Nesia had a firstborn animal—Rashi: priests in his house ate firstborn animals—and sent it to R. Ammi, who thought not to examine it. R. Zerika, or some say R. Yirmeyah, told him, etc. He then sent it to R. Yitzchak Nappacha, who thought not to examine it. R. Yirmeyah told him, etc. Taanit 14b: in R. Yehudah Nesia's days there was distress. He decreed thirteen fasts without answer and considered more. R. Ammi told him not to burden, etc. R. Abba son of R. Chiyya bar Abba said R. Ammi acted for himself—Rashi: he did not wish to fast—since R. Yochanan said they continue fasting until answered from heaven. There, 25b, near the end: he decreed a fast, rain fell after sunrise, and he considered completing it. R. Ammi told him, etc. There, 24a: R. Yehudah Nesia decreed a fast and prayed, but rain did not come. He said, “What a difference between Shmuel of Ramah”—for whom rain fell—“and Yehudah ben Gamliel, or between the generations, etc. Woe to one in whose days this happened!” He became distressed, and rain came. This R. Yehudah Nesia is Gamliel's son. It is puzzling that the events at 14 and 25 would concern the second R. Yehudah Nesia, while 24 concerns the first.

There appears some necessity for Tosafot's view that the nasi who asked R. Ammi was the grandson of R. Yehudah Nesia son of R. Gamliel son of our holy Rabbi. Nazir, beginning of chapter 4, 20b, near the end: Resh Lakish sat before R. Yehudah Nesia and said, etc. Avodah Zarah 6b: a sectarian sent the nasi a dinar on his festival day, while Resh Lakish sat before him. Arvei Pesachim 119a; Shabbat 119b, near the end; Bekhorot 22a; Moed Katan 20a; Niddah 41b: Resh Lakish said in R. Yehudah Nesia's name. Apparently Resh Lakish was his student. The chapter “Rabbi Eliezer of circumcision” has Resh Lakish in R. Yehudah HaNasi's name; apparently it should read Nesia. Jerusalem Moed Katan, chapter 3, halakhah 5: R. Yonah, R. Chiyya, and R. Shimon ben Lakish in R. Yudan Nesia's name. Chagigah 24b: R. Ammi said: Resh Lakish said. Jerusalem Berakhot, chapter 1, mishnah 1; Maaserot, chapter 1, halakhah 1; Kirah; Shekalim, chapter 1. R. Yehudah Nesia became angry with Resh Lakish, who fled; R. Yochanan went and brought him back: Yalkut, I Samuel, section 89. Thus R. Ammi was Resh Lakish's student. How could Resh Lakish's teacher, the nasi, ask R. Ammi, his student's student, and become his student's student's student? In my opinion this proof admits no answer. The truth is therefore that R. Yehudah Nesia son of R. Gamliel son of our holy Rabbi was Resh Lakish's teacher, while R. Ammi, Resh Lakish's student, taught that nasi's grandson. This resolves Tosafot's question in Eruvin 69a: a man went out with a signet ring. Seeing R. Yehudah Nesia, he covered it. The nasi said someone like this, who violated the Sabbath privately, may renounce his domain. Tosafot asks: did not R. Yehudah Nesia himself go out with a signet ring in Moed Katan 12b, where R. Ammi objected, because an important person is different, etc.? According to the above, R. Ammi objected to the nasi's grandson, while Eruvin concerns R. Yehudah Nesia son of R. Gamliel son of our holy Rabbi.

(e) R. Hillel, who fixed intercalation, was his son. R. Hoshaya Rabbah told him, “I heard from your father” [the checked Jerusalem Beitzah reads “Did you hear from your father?”]: this is the first R. Yehudah Nesia; see there. R. Oshaya visiting Rav Yehudah concerns the second R. Yehudah Nesia; see there. R. Yochanan asked R. Oshaya, who did not answer, but answered Resh Lakish. R. Yehudah Nesia told R. Oshaya, “Is R. Yochanan not a great man?”: Yevamot 57a. Berakhot 44a: R. Yochanan said to R. Yehudah Nesia. [In the checked Bavli he addresses the nasi’s household.] “Rav Chanin bar Abba”—it should read Rava—“Rav's son-in-law and Rav Chisda's father-in-law, eulogized him in Babylonia.” Surely this was written because Moed Katan 22b says a nasi died, and Rav Chisda told Rav Chanan bar Rava to overturn a mortar and demonstrate garment tearing. But whence that this nasi was R. Yehudah Nesia? Furthermore, he died in the Land of Israel; see immediately below. Jerusalem Berakhot, chapter 3, mishnah 1: when R. Yehudah Nesia, grandson of R. Yehudah Nesia, died, R. Chiyya bar Abba pushed R. Zeira and made him impure. Nazir, chapter 7, halakhah 1, has R. Chiyya pushing R. Zeira bar Ba; a scribal error, it should read R. Chiyya bar Ba pushing R. Zeira. When Nehorai—in Nazir, Nehoraynu [the checked Nazir text reads Yehudinai]—the nasi's sister, died, R. Chanina sent for R. Mana, who did not come; there. With him they ceased calling a nasi “Rabban”; see Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Elder. Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 38b, says Chizkiyah and Bar Kappara were tannaim and older than R. Yehudah Nesia. Gelilot Eretz Yisrael locates R. Yehudah HaNasi's burial at Mavnit; perhaps it should read R. Yehudah Nesia, since elsewhere it places our holy Rabbi's burial at Tzippori.

(f) Abba, Shmuel's father, sent before R. Yehudah Nesia; see there. R. Abba bar Mammal questioned him. R. Abba bar Zavda, Zeira, and R. Yitzchak Chakola, in R. Yehudah Nesia's name: Jerusalem Ketubot, chapter 2, halakhah 10 [2:9:4 in the checked edition]. End of Chalon has R. Yehudah Nesaya; end of HaBa Al Yevimto, Nasi. R. Yannai and R. Yochanan were sitting; R. Yehudah Nesia entered and asked: Jerusalem Yesh Nochalin, halakhah 1. R. Yannai and R. Simlai; see there. R. Simlai in R. Yehoshua ben Levi’s name—or some say R. Simlai and R. Yehoshua ben Levi in R. Yehudah Nesia’s name: Bekhorot 36b. [In the first version, the checked Bavli names both R. Simlai and R. Yehudah Nesia as transmitting in R. Yehoshua ben Levi’s name.] Rav Shemen bar Abba spoke before R. Yochanan, who went and stated it before the nasi: Niddah 52a. He asked Rav Shmuel bar Nachman; see there.
